files.body:
### Features

- **Links to Paperless work when Nextcloud reaches Paperless by a name of Docker or of your network.** The new optional setting *Address of Paperless in the browser* in *1 · Connection and ownership* holds the address that browsers open, such as `https://paperless.example.com`, while Nextcloud keeps sending its requests to the Paperless URL, such as `http://paperless:8000` in the network of Docker Compose. *Open in Paperless* and *Open Paperless* in Files, the notification of a file sent from Files, the entry of an import in the Activity app and the `url` of the metadata next to the archive take it; left empty, they take the Paperless URL as before. The next run writes the metadata once more with the new address.
- **A request that Paperless refuses during a run says what to do.** When Paperless refuses the API token, the account lacks a permission, a document went away during the run, Paperless or its proxy fails, or Nextcloud can't reach Paperless, can't resolve its name, waits too long or doesn't trust its certificate, the status and the report on the settings page explain in your language what happened and how to fix it, and the notification and the status API in English, instead of the bare English message of the HTTP client, which stays as a detail and in the log. The box of the errors links to the table *Messages and their fixes* of the troubleshooting page, which has a row for each of them. A Paperless without version 9 of its API is named in your language too.
- **A monitor reads the health of the mirror with a token that opens nothing else.** The new section *Health check for a monitor* on the settings page creates a token for Uptime Kuma, Home Assistant or any other monitor, shows it once beside the *Health check URL*, `/index.php/apps/paperless_sync/api/v1/health`, and revokes it again. The monitor sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and gets whether the mirror is healthy, its health, the state of the last run, the last success and the runs that failed in a row, without the error of a run and without an app password of an administrator, which opens every file and the administration of Nextcloud. A wrong token is refused and slowed down as for the webhook. The status API for administrators stays as it is; the guide shows the token in its examples for `curl`, Uptime Kuma and Home Assistant.
- **Write all copies again from the settings page.** A new button beside *Refresh* does what `occ paperless_sync:forget --all` does, for administrators without a shell, such as at a hoster of managed Nextcloud, and for the members of a group to which the page is delegated: after a question that says what it costs, the next runs download every document again, batch by batch, and write it in place of its copy. A copy that someone edited or that was damaged in Nextcloud gets the content of Paperless back, and keeps its path, its shares and its versions.

### Bug fixes

- **A deleted Nextcloud user leaves nothing behind.** When an administrator deletes a user in Nextcloud, Paperless Sync removes their line of **Tags that a user may see**, the lines of **Paperless users with another Nextcloud ID** that name them, and what the app kept of their archive, their inbox and the files that they sent to Paperless. Before, all of it stayed until someone saved the settings again, and a new account with the same ID got the documents of the old line. The documents of a Paperless user whose line named the deleted user now go by the usual rule, to the Nextcloud user with the same ID or else to the target user: give that Paperless user a new line or another owner in Paperless. When the deleted user is the target user, the administrators get a notification that every run fails until the settings name another target user.
- **The inbox no longer uploads a file a second time.** Before each upload, also the next attempt after a failed one, a run asks Paperless for a document with the content of the file, as *Send to Paperless* does, and ends the file as imported when Paperless has it, such as after an upload that Paperless received although its answer never came. A file that is renamed or moved inside the inbox, or whose folder is renamed, keeps its upload: a pending upload goes on at the new path, and a file kept after its import stays imported, so Paperless-ngx 3.x no longer gets a duplicate and 2.x no longer sends an imported file to the error folder. A file that Paperless refused still gets a new chance when it is renamed. In per-user ownership, a file with the same content as another user's document still goes up as a document of its own.
- **A failed inbox file never replaces another one in the error folder.** When the name is taken there, as when a scanner names every scan `scan.pdf` and two of them fail, the second one takes the next free number, `scan (2).pdf`, with its own `.error.txt`, whatever the conflict policy. Before, the default policy *Replace* deleted the earlier failed file, the only original of it, and overwrote its reason, and the policy *Skip* kept the second file in the inbox with a conflict.
- **A user of Nextcloud whose ID is all digits works like any other**, such as `1001` from LDAP. Before, every run with per-user ownership, with the documents that Paperless shares or with "Tags that a user may see" failed with an internal type error that named no setting as soon as such a user, also the target user, got documents or had a line, and the connection checklist warned that Nextcloud could not store their files. Now they get their documents, their inbox and their report as every other user does.
- **Tags that a user may see** now also finds a share of the archive with a Team that a user with tags is in, which shows them every document in it, as a share with a group does. A share with a conversation of Talk or a board of Deck, whose members Nextcloud doesn't name, is listed as one that may reach a user with tags: the connection checklist warns of it instead of passing, and the settings page and `occ paperless_sync:status` list it too. Without Talk, Deck or Teams, the check works as before.
- **A stored token that can no longer be decrypted no longer breaks Files.** After a restore or a move of Nextcloud with another `secret` in `config.php`, or with a damaged row of its credentials store, Files failed to load for every user, and the settings page that could take a new token failed too. Now such a token counts as none: Files, the settings page, the status API and the checks of *Administration → Overview* keep working, the settings say on top that the token has to be entered again, `occ paperless_sync:status` says so as well, also in its JSON output as `tokenUnreadable`, and the log has a warning. A webhook secret that can't be decrypted counts as none too, and a new one can be created. Files no longer reads and decrypts the token with every load, for every user: its menu and its note read the settings alone.
- The **Nextcloud target user ID** is saved as Nextcloud spells the account name, such as `dennis` when you type `Dennis`, as the users of the tables of the ownership and of the tags are. Before, another case reached the right folder, but the activity entries and the notifications of failed imports went to an ID that no user has, and the check of the shares for **Tags that a user may see** found none. The update stores a target user saved in another case as Nextcloud spells it, once. A save now also refuses a new target user that Nextcloud doesn't have, and keeps a saved one that is gone since, so that a schedule can always be paused.
- **A copy in the deleted folder no longer moves into a second one when its document shows up in the trash of Paperless.** A document that the missing scans had moved to `_Deleted/<day>/` and that then appeared in the trash of Paperless went to `_Deleted/<day>/_Deleted/<day>/…`. Now the copy stays where it is, and the run only marks the document as trashed.
- **The switches *Prefer Paperless archive versions* and *Skip Paperless inbox documents* explain themselves.** Each has a hint, which a screen reader reads with it, and a link to the guide: what an archive version is and what the originals bring instead, such as images or office documents and scans without a layer of text, and that the inbox there is that of Paperless, not the Nextcloud inbox, so a document with an inbox tag of Paperless waits until it is filed there.
- **A run of "Synchronize now" that the background jobs never start says so.** Before, the status said *Queued* for good, and the settings page kept asking for it, when the cron job of the system didn't run or Nextcloud lost the job. After 15 minutes, while no other run holds it back, the status says *Not started*, the bar of the buttons says so in the color of errors, with the last run of the background jobs of Nextcloud, so that you can check that they run, and the page stops asking. `occ paperless_sync:status` says the same.
- **A file sent to Paperless no longer stays pending for good when Paperless keeps refusing its new owner.** In per-user ownership, a refusal that repeats, such as 403 for an account that may no longer change the document or 400 for an owner that Paperless doesn't take, ends the import at once, and any other refusal a day after the upload: the document is in Paperless, so the sender hears that it is, with the reason why it keeps the owner that Paperless gave it, and may send the file again. A file of the inbox ends the same way, as imported, and the report of that run names the owner as an error once, instead of every run keeping the file in the inbox with the same error.
- **A sent file is no longer dropped as "deleted" when Nextcloud can't look it up for a moment.** When the lookup of a queued file fails while its user still exists, such as while a user backend like LDAP doesn't answer, the file waits for its next attempt, as after a failed upload, instead of ending with a notification that it was deleted, or, for a file of a rule of Flow, without reaching Paperless and without a word. A file that is gone, or whose sender's account was deleted, ends as before.
- **A file replaced in the inbox after its upload goes to Paperless with its new content.** When the import of a file failed, such as a damaged scan, and someone saved a repaired version under the same name before the next run, the run moved the repaired file to the error folder, next to the reason of the old content, and it never reached Paperless. Now it stays in the inbox, the report names the failure of the former content, and the next run uploads the new one.
- **A tag that Paperless lacks is no longer lost without a word when files go by *Send to Paperless* or a rule of Flow.** With *Create missing tags* off, such a file went to Paperless without the tag, and nobody learned of it. Now the sender, also the owner of the files of a rule, gets one notification, *Sent to Paperless without the tags …*, which names the tags and the files, and the Nextcloud log has a warning, as for the inbox.
- **A copy that a stopped run wrote is no longer a conflict forever.** With *Skip and report conflict*, a run that stopped between writing a new copy, or moving one, and saving its path, such as at a restart of the server, left a copy that every later run reported as `Nextcloud file conflict at …`, so the document was never updated or moved again. Now a file at the path of the document with the content of the app's copy, or with the content of the document by the checksum of Paperless, counts as the app's own when the copy that the app knows of is gone.
- **A copy that someone edited stays when its update failed before it began.** When Nextcloud refused to write the new content of a document into its copy, for a full quota, a locked file or a missing permission, the app still took the copy as its own, and a later run wrote the content of Paperless over an edit of it, also with *Skip and report conflict*. Such a copy now keeps its fingerprint, and the run reports the edit as a conflict and leaves the file.
- **A Paperless URL that redirects is named as such.** A URL that leads to a redirect, such as from `http://` to `https://` or from an old name to a new one, looked like a token that Paperless refused, and an upload through it reached Paperless without its file and failed after six attempts without a cause. Paperless Sync now follows no redirect: *Test connection*, a run and an upload say where the redirect leads and which URL to enter. A URL whose redirect the mirror followed so far has to be changed to that address.
- **The app names the databases that it supports.** The app info declares SQLite, MySQL or MariaDB, and PostgreSQL, so that Nextcloud and the App Store no longer offer it for Oracle, whose tables can't take the rows of the app.
- **A large document over a slow line is no longer cut off after three minutes.** The download of a document from Paperless and the upload of a file of the inbox stopped after 180 seconds, however much was still arriving, so a large scan over a slow uplink or a VPN failed in every run. Now a transfer goes on as long as it moves, and stops only after a minute below 1 KB a second, or after an hour. One that stops says so, with the document and the bytes that arrived, or with the file and its size, and the troubleshooting page explains it.
- **The icon of Paperless Sync matches the other icons of Nextcloud.** In the list of the administration settings, Paperless Sync showed its colored logo while every other section has a black icon, and the activity, its filter and the notifications showed the logo in color as well. They show the icon of the app as one black shape now, which turns white on the active entry and in the dark theme, as the icons of Nextcloud do. The colored logo stays on the page of the settings, in the README and on the website.
- **New documents reach the archive again on Nextcloud 33.0.11, 34.0.6, 35.0.3 and newer.** Since an update to one of these versions, every run ended with *Completed with errors* and `No permission to move …/.<name>.paperless-<hex>.part` for each document that wasn't in the archive yet, while the copies that were there stayed up to date ([#490](https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-sync/issues/490)). A new copy is still written into a hidden temporary file first and appears at its place only once it is complete, now in a way that these versions of Nextcloud allow, and a write that fails removes its temporary file again. Each failed run had left such a hidden file, which Files doesn't show, in the data folder of the target user: the first run after the update removes them from the archive and the error folder, once, and touches no other file. The [troubleshooting page](https://dennis-otto.github.io/paperless-sync/troubleshooting.html#hidden-part-files-in-the-archive) says how to remove them by hand elsewhere.
